chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (mercy of God be upon him) said: My father said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa said, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, on the authority of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, on the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, Musa son of 'Imran (peace be upon him) said: "O my Lord! I am pleased with what You have decreed, that You cause the elder to die and keep the young alive." Allah, the Mighty and High, replied: "O Musa! Are you not pleased with Me for being their Sustainer and Provider?" He said: "Of course, O Lord! You are the Best Custodian and the Best of Providers."
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Musa say to God regarding the death of the elderly and survival of the young?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Prophet Musa (AS) demonstrates *rida* (contentment) with the apparent disparity in divine decree regarding life and death, acknowledging God’s absolute sovereignty. Allah responds by affirming His dual role as *Raziq* (Sustainer) and *Kafil* (Guarantor), emphasizing that while decree is divine, provision and care are His continuous attributes. This dialogue underscores the Shia theological balance between accepting *qada* (decree) and trusting in *tawakkul* (reliance) on God’s ongoing sustenance.
